# Copilot Instructions for as16

## What This Project Is

**as16** is an assembler (and companion disassembler) for the RiSC-16 processor — a 16-bit RISC architecture. It parses assembly source using a Yacc/Bison grammar (`as.y`) compiled to C, and emits hex machine code. The disassembler (`disasm.c`) reverses the process.

## Build Commands

```bash
# Simple build (preferred)
make          # builds both `as16` and `disasm`
make clean

# CMake build
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build
```

## Test Commands

```bash
# Run the full test suite (CMake)
cd build && ctest -C Release

# Run a single test manually
./as16 test.asm
./as16 test_forward_relative_reference.asm
./as16 test_symbol_not_defined.asm   # expected to emit an error
```

The three `.asm` files in the root cover: normal assembly, forward relative branches, and undefined symbol error handling.

## Architecture

- **`as.y`** — Yacc/Bison grammar + embedded C actions. This is the heart of the assembler: lexer, parser, symbol table, fixup queue, and code emission all live here.
- **`as.h`** — Shared constants and structs: opcodes, bit-field positions, `Symbol_t`, `Fixup_t`, instruction limits.
- **`disasm.c`** — Standalone disassembler; reads hex/decimal machine code and prints mnemonics with addresses.
- **`y.tab.c` / `y.tab.h`** — Generated by Bison from `as.y`; do not edit directly.

## Key Conventions

### Single-Pass Assembly with Fixups
The assembler is single-pass. Forward references are queued in a `Fixup_t` array and resolved after all symbols are defined. Fixup types: `FIXUP_IMM7`, `FIXUP_IMM10`, `FIXUP_IMM6`, `FIXUP_IMM10_HI`, `FIXUP_REL7`.

### Instruction Encoding Helpers
Three helper functions in `as.y` encode instructions into 16-bit words:
- `rrr(op, rA, rB, rC)` — 3-register format
- `rri(op, rA, rB, imm7)` — register + 7-bit immediate
- `ri(op, rA, imm10)` — register + 10-bit immediate

All use the bit positions defined in `as.h`: `OP_SHIFT=13`, `RA_SHIFT=10`, `RB_SHIFT=7`.

### Instruction Set
8 real instructions (ADD, ADDI, NAND, LUI, SW, LW, BEQ, JALR) plus ~13 pseudo-instructions (NOP, HALT, LLI, MOVI, RET, PUSH, POP, J, CALL, INC, DEC, MOV, LWI) and assembler directives (`.fill`, `.space`, `EQU`).

Register aliases: `SP`=R7, `LR`=R6, `FP`=R5. Hex literals use `0x` or `$` prefix. Comments use `#` or `;`.

### Limits (all defined in `as.h`)
```c
#define MAX_CODE    1024   // max instructions
#define MAX_SYMBOLS 1024   // symbol table entries
#define MAX_FIXUPS  1024   // forward reference slots
```

### Grammar File is the Source of Truth
When adding instructions or pseudo-instructions, the grammar (`as.y`) is the only file to edit — it contains the lexer rules, parser grammar, and code-generation actions together. Run `make` to regenerate `y.tab.c`.
